key_insight: The paper reformulates phase-field fracture for composite shells as a modular constitutive operator built from four orthogonal strain invariants, enabling separate fibre, matrix/inter-fibre, and interaction damage channels with certified algebraic admissibility.
engineering_relevance: This gives shell analysts a more flexible and verifiable way to model fracture in curved fibre-reinforced structures, especially when curvature and fibre orientation create through-thickness damage patterns that a single midsurface field misses.
method: Geometrically exact Reissner–Mindlin shell kinematics with Green-Lagrange strain pulled back by the reference metric Cholesky factor
Exact invariant decomposition into four orthogonal channels with closure, tension–compression split, and channel-wise degradation
Certified admissible operator framework with plane-stress condensation, consistent tangent, and finite-element assembly expressed in channel potentials
evidence_signal: Numerical studies on notched IM7/8552 shells validate the method in thin and curved regimes and show sensitivity of damage and load capacity to fibre orientation and curvature.
watch_item: The framework depends on admissible constitutive operators and positive residual stiffness for regular condensation, so learned or custom laws must pass the certification checks.
paper_title: Mechanism-resolved phase-field fracture of composite shells with a certified admissible constitutive operator
